questions.question: A circle inscribed in a triangle ABC touches its sides AB, BC and AC at the points D, E and F, respectively. If AB = 18 cm, BC = 15 cm and AC = 13 cm, then the value of AD + BE + CF is:
questions.questionHtml: A circle inscribed in a triangle ABC touches its sides AB, BC and AC at the points D, E and F, respectively. If AB = 18 cm, BC = 15 cm and AC = 13 cm, then the value of AD + BE + CF is:
questions.solution:
Given:

AB = 18 cm, BC = 15 cm and AC = 13 cm,

Calculation:

We know, AD = AF, DB = BE, CE = FC

The perimeter of the triangle = AB + BC + AC = 18 + 15 + 13 = 46

That is, AD + AF + BD + BE + CE + CF = 46

Or, 2 × (AD + BE + CF) = 46

∴ AD + BE + CF = 23

questions.question: A, B and C are three points on a circle such that the angles subtended by the chord AB and AC at the centre O are 110° and 130°, respectively. The value of ∠BAC is:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C are three points on a circle such that the angles subtended by the chord AB and AC at the centre O are 110° and 130°, respectively. The value of ∠BAC is:
questions.solution:
from the following figure.

∠AOB = 110° and ∠AOC = 130°

As we know,

∠AOB + ∠AOC + ∠BOC = 360°

∠BOC = 360° - 110° - 130° = 120°

∠BAC = ∠BOC/2

∴ ∠BAC = 120°/2 = 60°

questions.question: In the figure, L is the centre of the circle, and ML is the perpendicular to LN. If the area of the triangle MLN is 36, then the area of the circle is:
questions.questionHtml: In the figure, L is the centre of the circle, and ML is the perpendicular to LN. If the area of the triangle MLN is 36, then the area of the circle is:
questions.solution:
In ΔLMN, LM = LN = r (Radius of the circle)

Area of right-angled ΔLMN = (1/2) × r × r

⇒ 36 = r2/2 ⇒ r2 = 72

∴ Area of the circle = πr2 = 72π

questions.solution:
Here, the major arc for the PQ chord is PRQ, hence, ∠PRQ = 55°

questions.question: The ratio in which a transverse common tangent drawn to two circles with radii 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively, divides the line joining their centres is:
questions.questionHtml: The ratio in which a transverse common tangent drawn to two circles with radii 4 cm and 6 cm, respectively, divides the line joining their centres is:
questions.solution:
In ∆AOC and ∆BMC, We have,  ∠A = ∠B = 90°( tangent and radius  at same point are perpendicular to each other)

∠AOC = ∠BMC ( OA and MB are perpendicular to the same line AB. So, OA || MB, Thus, by alternate angle theorem Angle AOC = Angle BMC)

Hence,  ∆AOC ≈ ∆BMC. so, \(\frac{AO}{BM}\)=\(\frac{OC}{MC}\)= \(\frac{4}{6}\) = \(\frac{2}{3}\), so the ratio = 2 : 3

questions.question: In the following figure, MN is a tangent to a circle with centre O at point A. If BC is a diameter and ∠ABC = 42°, then find the measure of ∠MAB.
questions.questionHtml: In the following figure, MN is a tangent to a circle with centre O at point A. If BC is a diameter and ∠ABC = 42°, then find the measure of ∠MAB.
questions.solution:
Given:

BC is a diameter

∠ABC = 42°

Concept used:

Alternate segment theorem = The angle between a tangent and a chord is equal to the angle in the alternate segment.

Diameter makes an angle of 90 degree on circumference

Calculation:

According to the concept,

∠BAC = 90°

So, ∠BCA = 180° - 42° - 90° 

⇒ 48°

Now, according to the concept,

∠MAB = ∠BCA

So, ∠MAB = 48°

∴ The measure of ∠MAB is 48°.

questions.question: Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point A, where P and Q are points on the circle. If the ∠PAQ = 70°, then the ∠AOP is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: Two tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O from an external point A, where P and Q are points on the circle. If the ∠PAQ = 70°, then the ∠AOP is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

∠PAQ = 70°

Concept:

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Calculation:

∠PAQ + ∠POQ + ∠OPA + ∠OQA = 360°

⇒ 70° + ∠POQ + 90° + 90° = 360°

⇒ ∠POQ = 360° - 70° - 90° - 90°

⇒ ∠POQ = 110°

⇒ ∠AOP = ∠AOQ = ∠POQ/2

⇒ ∠AOP = 110°/2

⇒ ∠AOP = 55°

∴ The value of ∠AOP is 55°.

questions.question: Distance of a chord JK from the centre is 7 cm. If diameter of this circle is 50 cm, then what will be length of this chord?
questions.questionHtml: Distance of a chord JK from the centre is 7 cm. If diameter of this circle is 50 cm, then what will be length of this chord?
questions.solution:
Diameter of circle = 50 cm, then Radius = OJ = 50/2 = 25 cm

In Δ JOP, OJ = Hypotenuse = 25, and OP = Perpendicular = 7

Apply Pythagoras Theorem, ⇒ OJ2 = OP2 + JP2 ⇒ 252 = 72 + JP2  ⇒ JP2 = 576 JP = 24

Length of chord JK = 2 × JP = 2 × 24 = 48 cm

questions.question: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 225 degree. What will be the angle made at the major arc of this circle?
questions.questionHtml: Sum of the angles made by a chord at the centre and on the major arc of a circle is 225 degree. What will be the angle made at the major arc of this circle?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

The angle subtended by a chord at the centre is always twice the angle subtended by it on the major arc.

Ratio of Angle at Centre : Angle on Major Arc = 2 : 1

Total Ratio Units = 2 + 1 = 3 units

Given: 3 units = 225°

1 unit = 225° ÷ 3 = 75°

∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.

Alternate Method

Given:

Sum of angle at the centre and angle on the major arc = 225°.

Formula Used:

Angle subtended by an arc at the centre is double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle.

Calculations:

Let the angle subtended by the chord at the major arc be x.

⇒ Angle subtended at the centre = 2x

⇒ x + 2x = 225°

⇒ 3x = 225°

⇒ x = 225° ÷ 3

⇒ x = 75°

∴ The correct answer is 75 degree.

Additional Information

Inscribed Angle Theorem

The angle subtended by an arc at the center is exactly twice the angle subtended by the same arc at any point on the circle's circumference (major arc).

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same chord or arc at different points on the same segment (major or minor) of the circle are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

The sum of the angle at the major arc and the angle at the minor arc subtended by the same chord is 180°, as they form opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral.

questions.question: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.questionHtml: AB is a chord of a circle in minor segment with center O. C is a point on the minor arc of the circle between the points A and B. The tangents to the circle at A and B meet at the point P. If ∠ACB = 102°, then what is the measure of ∠APB?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠ACB = 102°

Concept Used:

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Calculation:

Point D is taken on the major arc of the circle. Then, A & D, B & D, C & B, and A & C are joined.

∠ACB = 102°

Now,

∠ADB = (180 – 102)° = 78°

Now,

∠AOB = (78 × 2)° = 156°

Since OA = OB, ΔAOB is an isosceles triangle and ∠OBA = ∠OAB.

Now,

∠AOB + ∠OBA + ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OBA = (180 – 156)°

⇒ ∠OBA = 12°

Now,

∠OBA = 12°

∠OAB = 12°

Now,

∠OAP = ∠OAB + ∠BAP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAP = 78°

Now,

∠OBP = ∠OBA + ∠ABP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠ABP

⇒ ∠ABP = 78°

Now,

∠APB + ∠ABP + ∠BAP = 180°

⇒ ∠APB + 78° + 78° = 180°

⇒ ∠APB = 180° - (2 × 78)°

⇒ ∠APB = 24°

∴ The required measure of ∠APB is 24°.

questions.questionHtml: In a circle centered at O, a tangent AP is drawn from an external point. If OA = 13 cm and OP = 5cm, then the length of tangent AP is:
questions.solution:
Given 

OA = 13 cm 

OP = 5cm 

Formula Used 

(Hypotnuese)2 = (Perpendicular)2 + (Base)2

Calculation 

We know that, tangent makes right angle with center of circle 

⇒ ΔOPA is right angle triangle, ∠OPA = 90°  

⇒ (Hypotnuese)2 = (Perpendicular)2 + (Base)2

⇒ (OA)2 = (AP)2 + (OP)2

⇒ 132 = AP2 + 52 

⇒ AP = 12 cm

questions.question: The length of the direct common tangent is 24 cm for two circles whose radii are 16 cm and 6 cm. What is the distance between their centres?

The radius of the smaller circle, r2 =  1 cm

 \(24 = \sqrt{d^2-(16-6)^2}\)

Hence, the distance between their centers is 26 cm.

questions.solution:
∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB ⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × 50° ⇒ ∠AOB = 100°

Chords AB and CD of a circle, when produced, meet at a point P outside the circle. If AB = 6 cm, CD = 3 cm and PD = 5 cm

PA × PB = PC × PD

(6 + x) x = 8 × 5

questions.question: The radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 4 cm. If the distance between their centres is 25 cm, then the length of the transverse common tangent is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: The radii of the two circles are 7 cm and 4 cm. If the distance between their centres is 25 cm, then the length of the transverse common tangent is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of first circle (r1) = 7 cm

Radius of second circle (r2) = 4 cm

Distance between centers (d) = 25 cm

Formula used:

Length of transverse common tangent (T) = \(\sqrt{d^2 - (r_1 + r_2)^2}\)

Calculation:

T = \(\sqrt{25^2 - (7 + 4)^2}\)

⇒ T = \(\sqrt{625 - 121}\)

⇒ T = \(\sqrt{504}\)

⇒ T = 6√14 cm

∴ The correct answer is option 2.

questions.question: PA and PB are two tangents from a point P outside the circle with centre O. If A and B are points on the circle such that ∠APB = 100°, then ∠OAB is equal to:
questions.questionHtml: PA and PB are two tangents from a point P outside the circle with centre O. If A and B are points on the circle such that ∠APB = 100°, then ∠OAB is equal to:
questions.solution:
Given:

∠APB = 100°

O is the centre of the circle.

PA and PB are two tangents drawn from P outside the circle

Concept used:

A tangent to a circle forms a right angle with the circle's radius.

The Sum of all angles of a quadrilateral is 360°.

Calculation:

A tangent to a circle forms a right angle with the circle's radius

⇒ ∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90°

The Sum of all angles of a quadrilateral is 360°

⇒ ∠OAP + ∠OBP + ∠APB + ∠AOB = 360°

⇒ 90° + 90° + 100° + ∠AOB = 360°

⇒ ∠AOB = 360° - 280°

⇒ ∠AOB = 80°

In ΔAOB

⇒ ∠AOB + ∠OAB + ∠OBA = 180°

⇒ 80° + x + x = 180°

⇒ 2x = 100°

⇒ x = 50°

∴ The value of ∠OAB is 50°.

questions.questionHtml: In the given figure O is the centre of the circle. If angle PRQ = 64°, then what is the measure of angle OPQ?
questions.solution:
Given:

∠PRQ=64°

Concept Used:

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal.

The sum of the angles of a triangle is 180°.

Formula Used:

θ = α/2

where θ → Angle made by a chord at circumference of a circle,

α → Angle made by the same chord at the center of the circle

Calculations:

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Let ∠POQ = x, ∠OPQ = y

Chord PQ makes ∠PRQ at the circumference and ∠POQ at center of circle.

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 64° 

⇒ x = 128° 

In ΔPOQ,

OP = OQ

⇒ ∠OPQ = ∠OQP = y

Now, In ΔPOQ, 

∠ POQ + ∠OPQ + ∠OQP = 180° 

⇒ 128° + y + y = 180° 

⇒ 2y = 180° – 128° 

⇒ y = 52°/2

⇒ y = 26° 

∴ The value of ∠OPQ is 26°.

questions.questionHtml: Two circles with centers P and Q of radii 7 cm nd 3 cm, respectively, touch each other externally at a point A. BC is a direct common tangent to these two circles where B and C are the points on the circles respectively. The length of BC is:

Given

The radii of both circles are 3 cm and 7 cm

Both circles touch each other at point A externally

BC is the common tangent of both circles.

Calculation

Join P to Q and B. Join Q to C. Draw PM ⊥ CQ.

Now PM = BC, as they are opposite sides of rectangle PMBC.

⇒ PQ = PA +AM

⇒ 7 cm + 3 cm

⇒ 10 cm.

⇒ QM = CQ – CM

⇒ 7 cm – 3cm

⇒ 4 cm

⇒ PM = √{(PQ)2 - (QM)2}

⇒ √{(10)2 - (4)2} 

⇒ 2√ 21

⇒ PM = BC

⇒ 2√ 21 cm

∴ The correct answer is 2√ 21 cm.

questions.question: Let C be a circle with center O and PQ be the diameter of C. Let AB be a chord on C. If ∠QOB = 40°, ∠AOP = 80°, then find ∠AOB.
questions.questionHtml: Let C be a circle with center O and PQ be the diameter of C. Let AB be a chord on C. If ∠QOB = 40°, ∠AOP = 80°, then find ∠AOB.

Given:

∠QOB = 40º

∠AOP = 80º

Formula used:

The sum of all angle on a straight line is 180º.

Calculation:

∠QOB = 40º

∠AOP = 80º

Since PQ is the diameter, 

Let ∠AOB = xº

∠AOB + ∠AOP + ∠QOB = 180º (sum of angles on a straight line)

⇒ x + 80º + 40º = 180º

⇒ x + 120º = 180º

⇒ x = 180º - 120º

⇒ x = 60º

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: If angle made by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 50 degree, then what will be the angle made by same chord on the minor arc of this circle?
questions.questionHtml: If angle made by a chord on the major arc of a circle is 50 degree, then what will be the angle made by same chord on the minor arc of this circle?
questions.solution:
Concept Used:

In a circle, the following property holds: the angle that a chord subtends on the major arc is 180 degrees minus the angle that the same chord subtends on the minor arc. This is due to the fact that any point on a circle defines an angle of 360 degrees.

Calculation:

So, if the angle made by a chord on the major arc is ∠ACB = 50°, 

then the angle that the same chord makes on the minor arc of the

circle would be  ∠ACB = 180 - 50 = 130°.

∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The length of a common external tangent to two circles of an equal radius of 5 units is equal to the diameter of the circle. Which of the following can be the distance between the centres of the circles in units?
questions.questionHtml: The length of a common external tangent to two circles of an equal radius of 5 units is equal to the diameter of the circle. Which of the following can be the distance between the centres of the circles in units?

questions.question: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. If C is any point on the circle such that ∠BAC = 42°, then find the measure of ∠BOC.
questions.questionHtml: AB is a diameter of a circle with centre O. If C is any point on the circle such that ∠BAC = 42°, then find the measure of ∠BOC.
questions.solution:
Given:

Diameter = AB 

∠BAC = 42°

Concept:

Angle in a semi-circle is a right angle. 

The Sum of all the angles in a triangle is 180°. 

Angles opposite to equal sides are equal in measure. 

Calculation:

In triangle ABC, ∠A + ∠B + ∠C = 180°      [Angle sum property]

⇒ 42° + ∠B + 90° = 180°                           [Angle in a semi-circle is 90°]    

⇒  ∠B =  180° - 90°- 42° = 48° 

In triangle BOC,  ∠OBC + ∠BOC + ∠BCO = 180°

⇒  48° +  48° + ∠BOC = 180°     [Angles opposite to equal sides are equal] 

⇒ ∠BOC = 180° - 48° -  48°        [ BO = CO = r] 

∴ ∠BOC = 84° 

Shortcut Trick The angle made on the center by a chord is double the angle made on the circumference by the same chord.

∠BOC = 2∠BAC = 2 × 42° 

⇒ 84° 

∴ The required angle is 84°.

questions.question: A tangent is drawn from a point P to a circle, which meets the circle at T such that PT = 8 cm. A secant PAB intersects the circle in points A and B. If PA = 5 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the chord AB?
questions.questionHtml: A tangent is drawn from a point P to a circle, which meets the circle at T such that PT = 8 cm. A secant PAB intersects the circle in points A and B. If PA = 5 cm, what is the length (in cm) of the chord AB?
questions.solution:
Given:

PT = 8 cm

PA = 5 cm

Concept used:

Tangent secant theorem

PT2 = PA × PB

Calculation:

We know that,

PT2 = PA × PB

⇒ (8)2 = 5 × PB

⇒ 64 = 5PB

⇒ PB = (64/5)

⇒ PB = 12.8 cm

Then,

AB = (12.8 – 5) = 7.8 cm

∴ The length of chord AB is 7.8 cm 

Shortcut Trick PT2 = PA × PB

⇒ (8)2 = 5 × PB

⇒ 64 = 5PB

⇒ PB = 12.8 cm

Then,

AB = (12.8 – 5) = 7.8 cm

questions.question: The distance between the centres of two equal circle each of radius 4 cm is 17 cm. The length of a transverse tangent is:
questions.questionHtml: The distance between the centres of two equal circle each of radius 4 cm is 17 cm. The length of a transverse tangent is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of 1st circle = 4 cm

Radius of 2nd circle = 4 cm

Distance between the centres of two circles = 17 cm

Formula used:

(Length of transverse tangent)2 = [(distance between the centres)2 – (r1 + r2)2]

Where r1 and r2 are the radii of two circles.

Calculation: 

Let the transverse tangent be PQ and distance between the centres be AB

Let r1 and r2 be the radii of the circles

According to the formula

⇒ (PQ)2 = (AB)2 – (r1 + r2)2

⇒ (PQ)2 = (17)2 – (4 + 4)2

⇒ (PQ)2 = 289 – 64

⇒ (PQ)2 = 225

⇒ PQ = √225

⇒ PQ = 15 cm

∴ The length of a transverse tangent is 15 cm

questions.question: Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle of diameter 20 cm. The length of one chord is 16 cm and the distance between the two chords is 12 cm. The length of the other chord is:
questions.questionHtml: Two parallel chords are drawn in a circle of diameter 20 cm. The length of one chord is 16 cm and the distance between the two chords is 12 cm. The length of the other chord is:
questions.solution:
Calculation:

AB and PQ are two chords and O is the centre of the circle.

M is the mid-point of AB and N is the mid-point of PQ.

OB = OQ = 10 cm (radius of the circle)

AB = 16 cm and MN = 12 cm

Let OM = x, then

ON = (12 - x) cm

In ΔMOB

(OB)2 = (OM)2 + (MB)2

⇒ OM2 = 100 - 64

⇒ OM = √36

⇒ OM = 6

⇒ NQ = √64

⇒ NQ = 8

questions.question: A transverse common tangent is drawn to two circles of radius 8.5 cm and 5.5 cm. The centres of the two circles are 18 cm apart. What is the length (in cm) of the tangent?
questions.questionHtml: A transverse common tangent is drawn to two circles of radius 8.5 cm and 5.5 cm. The centres of the two circles are 18 cm apart. What is the length (in cm) of the tangent?
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of two circles are = 8.5 cm and 5.5 cm

Distance between the centre of the two circles = 18 cm

Formula Used:

The length of a transverse common tangent = \(\sqrt{d^2 - (r_{1} + r_{2})^2}\)

Where, d = distance between the centre of two circles

r1 and r2 = radius of the circles

Calculation:

⇒ Length of the tangent = \(\sqrt{18^2 - (8.5 + 5.5)^2}\)

⇒ Length of the tangent = \(\sqrt{324 - 196}\) = \(\sqrt{128}\)

⇒ Length of the tangent = \(8\sqrt{2}\) cm

∴ The correct answer is \(8\sqrt{2}\) cm. Option 3).

questions.question: Two chords AB and CD of a circle are produced to intersect each other at a point P outside the circle. If AB = 7 cm, BP = 4.2 cm and PD = 2.8 cm, then the length of CD is:
questions.questionHtml: Two chords AB and CD of a circle are produced to intersect each other at a point P outside the circle. If AB = 7 cm, BP = 4.2 cm and PD = 2.8 cm, then the length of CD is:
questions.solution:
Given

PB = 4.2 cm and AB = 7 cm

AP = 4.2 + 7 = 11.2

PD = 2.8 cm and Let CD = x.

PC = 2.8 + x

As we know,

AP × PB = PC × PD

11.2 × 4.2 = (x + 2.8) × 2.8 

⇒ x + 2.8 = (11.2 × 4.2) / 2.8

⇒ x + 2.8 = 16.8

⇒ x = 16.8 – 2.8

⇒ x = 14 cm

questions.question: Points A and B are on a circle with centre O. PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. If PA and PB are inclined to each other at 42°, then find the measure of ∠OAB.
questions.questionHtml: Points A and B are on a circle with centre O. PA and PB are tangents to the circle from an external point P. If PA and PB are inclined to each other at 42°, then find the measure of ∠OAB.
questions.solution:
Consider the quadrilateral AOBP, 

∠A + ∠O + ∠B + ∠P = 360° ⇒ 90° + ∠O + 90° + 42° = 360° ⇒ ∠O = 360° - 90° - 90° - 42° ⇒ ∠O = 138°

ΔOAB is an isosceles triangle since OA and OB are the radii of the circle so, ∠OAB = ∠OBA = R° (let)

2R° + 138° = 180° ⇒ 2R° = 42° ⇒ R = 21° ⇒ ∠OAB = 21°

questions.question: Two circles of radii 3 units and r units, respectively, have a 6 units distance between their centers. If the length of the direct common tangent is \(\sqrt35\) units, then the value of r is ________ units.
questions.questionHtml: Two circles of radii 3 units and r units, respectively, have a 6 units distance between their centers. If the length of the direct common tangent is \(\sqrt35\) units, then the value of r is ________ units.
questions.solution:
Given:

Radius of the first circle = 3 units

Radius of the second circle = r units

Distance between centers = 6 units

Length of the direct common tangent = √35 units

Formula used:

Length of direct common tangent = √(d2 - (r1 - r2)2)

Calculation:

√35 = √(62 - (3 - r)2)

⇒ 35 = 36 - (3 - r)2

⇒ (3 - r)2 = 36 - 35 = 1

⇒ 3 - r = ±1

⇒ r = 3 + 1 = 4 units OR

⇒ r = 3 - 1 = 2 units

So, the circle radius can be 2 units or 4 units. Since 2 units is not in the option, the correct answer will be 4 units.

∴ The correct answer is option (3).

questions.question: Two concentric circles are of radii 13 cm and 5 cm. The length of chord which touches the smaller circle is:
questions.questionHtml: Two concentric circles are of radii 13 cm and 5 cm. The length of chord which touches the smaller circle is:
questions.solution:
Given:

Two concentric circle are of radii 13 cm and 5 cm respectively.

Formula:

Hypotensue2 = Base2 + Perpendicular2

Calculation:

See the figure PQ touches the smaller circle and OM is perpendicular to QP which divides the PQ into two equal parts.

OM = 5 (radius of smaller circle)

OP = 13 (radius of bigger circle)

In right angled Δ OPM

(OP)2 = (OM)2 + (PM)2

⇒ 132 = 52 + (PM)2

⇒ (PM)2 = 169 - 25 

⇒ PM = √144

⇒ PM = 12

Now,

PQ = 2PM

⇒ PQ = 2 × 12

⇒ PQ = 24 cm

∴ The length of the chord which touches the smaller circle is 24 cm.
